_comment: The iTop branches this extension claims to support, and the PHP versions each is
tested on. This file is the single source of truth: the CI matrix is computed from
it, and every prose copy of the claim is checked against it rather than maintained
beside it.
Three such copies exist, because a link is not possible in any of them: the README's
Requirements table (this directory does not ship in the release archive), the Hub
listing's compatibility block (text somebody pastes into a web form) and the sentence
inside extension.xml's <description>, which the iTop setup shows to whoever installs
the module. The markdown ones are delimited by a supported-versions:begin/end pair;
ModuleMetadataTest::testProseAgreesWithTheDeclaredSupport reads all three and fails on
any disagreement with this file, or with composer.json for the PHP range. Edit here,
not there.
A branch names a minor (3.2), never a patch. CI resolves the latest patch of that
branch at run time, so a new 3.2.x published by Combodo is exercised by the next
scheduled run without anyone editing anything - which is the point: the version we
break on is usually the one released after we last looked.
branch           the iTop minor, as it appears in the tag names of Combodo/iTop
php              PHP versions to install that branch on. Two is enough: the floor
and the ceiling of what composer.json allows. The middle version
is covered by the unit matrix in ci.yml.
allow_prerelease resolve to an alpha/beta/rc when the branch has no stable patch
yet. True for a branch we intend to support at its GA and want to
be told about early; never for one users are already running.
pin              an exact tag, when a resolved patch is known broken and the
failure is not ours. Temporary by nature: say why, in this file.
3.3 is deliberately absent, and its absence is not a claim that the module fails
there. Nothing has ever been installed on 3.3 - not CI, not the sandbox - and a
branch named here is a branch the README, the Hub listing and the setup wizard all
tell an operator is tested. Naming one that is not is the single thing this file
exists to prevent. Add the entry once a 3.3 install has actually been exercised;
allow_prerelease is there for exactly that first look.
